items.text: Kwame Raoul was sworn in as Illinois attorney general in 2019 and began a second term in 2023. He began his legal career as a Cook County prosecutor and later became a partner at two national corporate law firms. He served in the Illinois Senate from 2004 to 2019 and chaired the Judiciary Committee. There he sponsored laws to abolish the death penalty and require background checks on private gun sales.

sentences.text: Kwame Raoul was sworn in as Illinois attorney general in 2019 and began a second term in 2023.
He began his legal career as a Cook County prosecutor and later became a partner at two national corporate law firms.
He served in the Illinois Senate from 2004 to 2019 and chaired the Judiciary Committee.
There he sponsored laws to abolish the death penalty and require background checks on private gun sales.

items.text: In office, Raoul has filed more than 50 lawsuits against the Trump administration, protecting roughly $6.6 billion in federal funding for Illinois. His lawsuits preserved money for disaster relief and medical research. He also sued to stop the administration from withholding $54 million in crime victim aid. He joined a lawsuit challenging new mail-in voting rules. He helped sue to stop an attempt to end birthright citizenship.

items.text: Raoul created the state’s first Organized Retail Crime Task Force and leads the Illinois Internet Crimes Against Children Taskforce. He secured a $7.4 billion settlement from his lawsuit against Purdue Pharma over opioids. His office negotiated a $140 million cut to a Nicor Gas rate increase request. His campaign says he has worked to expand access to emergency and medication abortion, and his Worker Protection Unit has secured millions of dollars in owed wages for workers.
